children: Among the risks outlined in Anthropic's filing is losing control of powerful AI systems, which the company's founders said "could be a global security threat of the first order."
They added that they plan to preserve Anthropic's unique culture of "radical internal honesty" in part by keeping its staff relatively small.

The founders outlined a philanthropically-inclined culture, in which each employee is offered a 1:1 match from the company of Anthropic equity they pledge to charity. All seven co-founders have already pledged 80% of their equity to charity.

In addition to personal charitable giving, they said the company has set aside 5% of its equity in a fund for the public good, and will set aside an additional 2% for each 50% increase in share price from the prior contribution, at the board's discretion. "Our ability to have a positive impact on the world scales in relation to our reach and stature as a successful company," they wrote.
This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
